title: My Favourite Arcade Games – Commodore 64 & Amiga Ports Reviewed
summary: A personal look at favourite 80s arcade games and how they translated to the Commodore 64 and Amiga, comparing gameplay, performance, and overall experience across platforms.
description:
This video explores a selection of classic arcade games from the 1980s and examines how they were adapted for the Commodore 64 and Amiga. Featuring titles such as Dragon’s Lair, Out Run, After Burner, Space Harrier, R-Type, Golden Axe, Double Dragon, Rolling Thunder, and Street Fighter, it combines personal reflection with detailed comparison.

Arcade hardware delivered speed, scale, and spectacle that home systems often struggled to replicate. As a result, many of these conversions required significant changes, whether through reduced visuals, altered gameplay, or entirely different design approaches. In some cases, the Commodore 64 versions prioritised playability over accuracy, while the Amiga often aimed to preserve the look and feel of the originals.

The video highlights how each version performs, what was lost or gained in translation, and how these games hold up today. It offers insight into the challenges of porting arcade experiences to home computers and why these titles remain memorable despite their differences.

summary: Revisiting the forgotten Commodore 64C Toolbox tapes from the Light Fantastic pack: The Image System, The Music System, SEUCK, Typing Tutor and the Toolbox Audio Tape.
description: In 1989 a brand-new Commodore 64C Light Fantastic pack came loaded with games, a Datasette, joystick, 3D glasses and the Cheetah Defender light gun, but also five easy-to-overlook yellow Toolbox cassettes. This Retro Special goes back to The Image System, The Music System, Shoot ’Em Up Construction Kit (SEUCK), Typing Tutor and the Toolbox Audio Tape to see what they actually offered. The Image System provides drawing and picture-manipulation tools; The Music System combines keyboard, multitrack and synthesiser features; SEUCK lets users build playable shoot-’em-ups; Typing Tutor covers keyboard accuracy and finger positioning; and the Toolbox Audio Tape guides a new C64C owner through connecting and starting the computer. title: Retro Games That Offered a Porsche, Swords & £25,000! | C64, Spectrum & Amiga
summary: Real 1980s retro gaming competitions: a Porsche 924, £25,000 cash, Wilkinson swords, Egyptian holidays, a helicopter flight and the players who won.
description:
Back in the 1980s, buying a computer game could mean a chance to win a Porsche 924, £25,000 in cash, an engraved Wilkinson Sword, a holiday to Egypt or even a helicopter flight. This Cheeky Commodore Gamer documentary investigates the extraordinary real-world prizes offered with Commodore 64, ZX Spectrum and Amiga games, using original competition adverts, magazines, surviving prizes and accounts of the winners.

From Hareraiser and its golden hare to Domark’s Eureka! £25,000 challenge, Quo Vadis, Spirit of the Stones and The Staff of Karnath, discover how ambitious treasure hunts became a selling point for 8-bit games. The investigation also covers Psytron, Kokotoni Wilf, Moon Cresta, William Wobbler, Lancelot, Murder on the Atlantic, Explora / Chrono Quest and Eye of Horus.

Hear the gruesome Friday the 13th cassette sound-effects competition, learn why Gladiator gave away real Wilkinson swords, and revisit the famous bugs of Jet Set Willy and the young Doomdark’s Revenge winner who telephoned Beyond Software from his headmaster’s office. The closing montage includes Splat!, the Ket Trilogy, Pimania’s golden sundial and Gyron’s Porsche competition.

Some winners have been identified and their prizes photographed; other competition results remain unconfirmed. Watch the story, jump to individual chapters or follow the verified CCG game-page links for more background.

title: Friday the 13th (1986) – Commodore 64 Horror Sound Effects Quiz
summary: Can you identify ten gruesome horror sounds from Domark’s original 1986 Friday the 13th C64 cassette competition? Five Eureka colour monitors were at stake.
description: Friday the 13th: The Computer Game was released for Commodore 64 (C64) by Domark in 1986. The original cassette included ten grisly BBC Enterprises sound effects as part of a horror audio competition. Match the noises to the clues, revisit Camp Crystal Lake and Jason Voorhees, and find out how a home-computer game offered five Eureka colour monitors as prizes. The historical contest is closed, but the ten-sound challenge lives on in this Cheeky Commodore Gamer video.

editorialSections.title: Friday the 13th on the Commodore 64: the forgotten 1986 sound effects competition
paragraphs: Domark’s Friday the 13th: The Computer Game arrived on the Commodore 64 in 1986, bringing Jason Voorhees and Camp Crystal Lake to home computers. But the original cassette offered more than the game: it also included a horror sound effects competition using recordings supplied by BBC Enterprises.

Players were asked to identify ten gruesome noises and match each one to a description from the competition entry form. The first five correct entries stood to win a Eureka colour monitor. The packaging was memorable too, with two novelty blood capsules included in the original release.

This Cheeky Commodore Gamer video revisits the original C64 cassette audio as a standalone ten-sound quiz. Listen closely and see whether you can work out clues such as “Jason has a meaty meal” and “Madam La Guillotine makes her mark”. You will need your ears, a little imagination and a reasonably strong stomach.

The original competition is long closed, but you can still take the challenge. Watch the Friday the 13th C64 quiz on YouTube, then leave your score in the video comments. Did you recognise all ten sound effects, and do you remember the original cassette release?
